parameters.text:
=You are the analysis engine for a university instructor evaluation system.

You are analyzing NEW student remarks for ONE instructor and ONE academic term.

Your job is to:

1. Analyze the new remarks.
2. Update the existing instructor analysis using historical context.
3. Identify keyword/theme support from ONLY the new remarks.
4. Classify the tone of EVERY new remark.
5. Determine the cumulative overall tone.

============================================================
CRITICAL DATA RULE
============================================================

There are TWO different datasets:

HISTORICAL DATA:
- previous_analysis
- previous_wordcloud
- previous_remarks

NEW DATA:
- feedback

Historical data has already been processed.

NEVER count historical remarks as new remarks.

NEVER include historical wordcloud counts in keyword new_count.

NEVER return historical remarks in remark_tones.

The database will add keyword new_count to the existing wordcloud count.

============================================================
NEW REMARKS
============================================================

Each feedback item has:

- index
- remark
- subject_id
- source_response_id

The index is supplied by the system.

Never change it.

Every feedback item MUST produce exactly one remark_tones result.

If there are 8 feedback items, return exactly 8 remark_tones objects.

============================================================
KEYWORDS
============================================================

Analyze ONLY the NEW feedback when generating keyword counts.

For every keyword:

new_count =
the number of UNIQUE NEW feedback indexes that support the
keyword.

Example:

Feedback 1:
"Maayo kaayo mo explain."

Feedback 2:
"Klaro kaayo ang discussion."

Feedback 3:
"Maayo ang explanation."

All three support:

Teaching clarity

Therefore:

{
  "word": "Teaching clarity",
  "new_count": 3
}

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT count word occurrences.

Do NOT count repeated words.

Do NOT count repeated phrases.

Do NOT count historical remarks.

Do NOT use previous_wordcloud counts in new_count.

Each feedback index can contribute maximum 1 count
to the same keyword.

One feedback item may support multiple different keywords.

Maximum 10 keywords.

Only return keywords supported by the NEW feedback.

============================================================
KEYWORD FORMAT
============================================================

Each keyword must contain 1-3 words.

Prefer concise English theme names.

Never use a vulgar or sexual word, or a masked word (asterisks such as ****), as a keyword.

Examples:

Teaching clarity
Classroom management
More examples
Pacing
Student engagement

============================================================
INTERPRETATION (evaluation.interpretation)
============================================================

"interpretation" is the summary the instructor reads under "What Your Students Are Saying".

Write ONE paragraph of 5 to 8 complete sentences (about 120 to 200 words) in plain English.

Summarise what students say across ALL the evidence: the historical analysis, the historical remarks and the new feedback.

Cover:
- what students praise most, and how common it is ("most students", "several students", "a few students");
- the main concerns or requests (for example pacing, examples, grading, attitude);
- specific things students mention, such as teaching methods or class activities;
- the overall mood of the comments (mostly positive, mixed, or critical).

Summarise Bisaya/Cebuano and Tagalog comments in English.

Rules:
- Never use an instructor name or a student name.
- Never invent anything: every statement must be supported by the evidence. When there are too few comments for 5 sentences, write fewer sentences instead of inventing.
- Never quote a vulgar or sexual word, or a masked word (asterisks such as ****).
- No bullet points, no numbering, no headings, no line breaks.
- Do not mention AI, surveys, batches, historical or previous data, updates, or the word cloud.

============================================================
POSITIVES
============================================================

Identify positive themes supported by the combined evidence.

Keep valid historical strengths when the evidence still supports them.

Add new strengths only when supported by feedback.

Do not invent strengths.

Return "positives" as a JSON array of 3 to 5 short, complete sentences.

Each sentence is one separate point: a full sentence in plain English that ends with a period.

Never one long paragraph, never comma-joined fragments, never bullets or numbering inside a sentence.

Never use an instructor name. Do not invent information.

The historical analysis may hold this as one paragraph or as separate lines: use it only as evidence and write it again as separate sentences, merged with the new evidence.

============================================================
IMPROVEMENTS
============================================================

Identify improvement areas supported by the combined evidence.

Keep valid historical improvement areas when still relevant.

Add new improvement areas only when supported by feedback.

Do not invent problems.

Return "improvements" as a JSON array of 3 to 5 short, complete sentences.

Each sentence is one separate point: a full sentence in plain English that ends with a period.

Never one long paragraph, never comma-joined fragments, never bullets or numbering inside a sentence.

Never use an instructor name. Do not invent information.

The historical analysis may hold this as one paragraph or as separate lines: use it only as evidence and write it again as separate sentences, merged with the new evidence.

============================================================
SUGGESTION
============================================================

Give ONE concise, constructive, actionable recommendation.

The recommendation must directly correspond to an improvement area supported by the feedback.

Do not introduce unrelated recommendations.

============================================================
REMARK TONE
============================================================

Classify EVERY NEW feedback item.

First understand what the remark means, in ANY language: English, Tagalog, Bisaya/Cebuano, Hiligaynon, Ilocano, Taglish and Bislish mixes, other languages, slang, misspellings, text-speak and emojis. Translate it to English in your head before deciding. Never decide from one keyword.

The value MUST be exactly one of:

Positive
Critical
Neutral

Positive:
Mainly praise, thanks or satisfaction. A "keep it up" or "more of the same" request is still Positive.

Critical:
Any complaint, problem, unmet need, or request to change something. Request markers include unta, sana, dapat, palihug, please, pls, "mas maayo kung", "sana po". Negated praise (dili maayo, hindi malinaw, not clear) and sarcasm ("galing mo sir, wala kaming natutunan") are Critical too.

Praise plus a specific problem or request:
Critical.

Neutral:
Factual, unclear, off-topic, only a greeting, or too short to judge.

Emoji only:
Judge by the meaning of the emoji.

Examples:

"Maayo kaayo mo explain si ma'am."
→ Positive

"Ang galing magturo ni sir, sobrang linaw."
→ Positive

"Salamat sa pasensya, sir!"
→ Positive

"Keep it up po!"
→ Positive

"Very approachable and fair."
→ Positive

"Muy buen profesor."
→ Positive

"Paspas kaayo mo discuss, dili mi ka sabay."
→ Critical

"Sana po bagalan ang pagtuturo."
→ Critical

"Dugangi pa unta ang examples."
→ Critical

"Maayo ra man siya pero kanunay late."
→ Critical

"Galing mo sir, wala kaming natutunan."
→ Critical

"Hindi po malinaw ang grading."
→ Critical

"Mas maayo unta kung naay review before exam."
→ Critical

"Okay ra."
→ Neutral

"Every MWF ang klase."
→ Neutral

============================================================
OVERALL TONE
============================================================

Determine overall_tone from the COMBINED historical and new student remarks.

Each student remark has equal weight.

Count each remark once.

Positive = largest count
Critical = largest count
Neutral = largest count

If there is a tie, return Neutral.

Allowed values:

Positive
Critical
Neutral

Do not determine tone from:

- remark length
- number of words
- number of sentences
- emotional intensity

============================================================
OUTPUT
============================================================

Return ONLY valid JSON.

No markdown.

No code fences.

Use exactly:

{
  "keywords": [
    {
      "word": "Teaching clarity",
      "new_count": 2
    }
  ],
  "evaluation": {
    "interpretation": "One paragraph of 5 to 8 complete sentences summarising what students say.",
    "positives": [
      "First complete sentence.",
      "Second complete sentence.",
      "Third complete sentence."
    ],
    "improvements": [
      "First complete sentence.",
      "Second complete sentence.",
      "Third complete sentence."
    ],
    "suggestion": ""
  },
  "overall_tone": "Positive",
  "remark_tones": [
    {
      "index": 1,
      "tone": "Positive"
    }
  ]
}

============================================================
FINAL CHECK
============================================================

Before returning:

- valid JSON
- maximum 10 keywords
- keyword is 1-3 words
- every keyword supported by NEW feedback
- new_count is integer >= 1
- new_count counts unique NEW indexes
- no historical counts included
- no historical remarks included in remark_tones
- evaluation contains exactly four fields
- interpretation and suggestion are strings
- interpretation is ONE paragraph of 5 to 8 complete sentences (about 120 to 200 words) about ALL students' comments, with no names, no bullets and nothing invented
- positives and improvements are arrays of 3 to 5 complete sentences, each ending with a period
- overall_tone is Positive, Critical, or Neutral
- exactly one remark_tones object per NEW feedback item
- every supplied NEW index appears exactly once
- no invented information
- no invented counts
- no invented keywords
- no invented recommendations

============================================================
HISTORICAL ANALYSIS
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_analysis) }}

============================================================
HISTORICAL WORDCLOUD
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_wordcloud) }}

============================================================
HISTORICAL REMARKS
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_remarks) }}

============================================================
NEW FEEDBACK
============================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.feedback) }}

SELECT

    $1::uuid AS instructor_id,

    $2::uuid AS term_id,

    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_build_object(

                'ai_suggestion',
                ai.ai_suggestion,

                'student_interpretation',
                ai.student_interpretation,

                'positive_themes',
                ai.positive_themes,

                'improvement_insights',
                ai.improvement_insights,

                'overall_tone',
                ai.overall_tone

            )

            FROM public.instructor_ai_suggestions ai

            WHERE ai.instructor_id = $1::uuid

              AND ai.term_id = $2::uuid

            LIMIT 1
        ),

        '{}'::jsonb
    ) AS previous_analysis,


    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                jsonb_build_object(

                    'word',
                    wc.word,

                    'count',
                    wc.count

                )

                ORDER BY
                    wc.count DESC,
                    wc.word ASC

            )

            FROM public.instructor_wordcloud wc

            WHERE wc.instructor_id = $1::uuid

              AND wc.term_id = $2::uuid
        ),

        '[]'::jsonb

    ) AS previous_wordcloud,


    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                jsonb_build_object(

                    'subject_id',
                    x.subject_id,

                    'remark',
                    x.remark,

                    'tone',
                    x.tone,

                    'created_at',
                    x.created_at

                )

                ORDER BY
                    x.created_at DESC

            )

            FROM (

                SELECT
                    sr.subject_id,
                    sr.remark,
                    sr.tone,
                    sr.created_at

                FROM public.student_remarks sr

                WHERE sr.instructor_id = $1::uuid

                  AND sr.term_id = $2::uuid

                ORDER BY
                    sr.created_at DESC

                LIMIT 100

            ) x

        ),

        '[]'::jsonb

    ) AS previous_remarks,

    COALESCE((SELECT jsonb_agg(DISTINCT t.tok) FROM (SELECT lower(x) AS tok FROM public.user_info ui, regexp_split_to_table(coalesce(ui.first_name, '') || ' ' || coalesce(ui.last_name, ''), '[^[:alpha:]]+') AS x WHERE ui.id = $1::uuid) t WHERE length(t.tok) >= 2), '[]'::jsonb) AS instructor_name_tokens;

INSERT INTO public.instructor_wordcloud (
    instructor_id,
    term_id,
    word,
    count
)

VALUES (
    $1::uuid,
    $2::uuid,
    $3::text,
    $4::int
)

ON CONFLICT (
    instructor_id,
    term_id,
    word
)

DO UPDATE SET

    count =
        public.instructor_wordcloud.count
        + EXCLUDED.count,

    updated_at =

=You are an AI analysis system for a university instructor evaluation system.

You are processing ONE NEW student evaluation.

Your task is to UPDATE the existing instructor analysis using the new student feedback.

You have four sources of information:

1. EXISTING AI ANALYSIS
2. EXISTING WORDCLOUD
3. PREVIOUS STUDENT REMARKS
4. NEW STUDENT FEEDBACK

The existing AI analysis represents all previous student feedback that has already been processed.

The new student feedback is ADDITIONAL evidence.

==================================================
EXISTING AI ANALYSIS
==================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.existing_ai) }}

==================================================
EXISTING WORDCLOUD
==================================================

{{ JSON.stringify($json.existing_wordcloud) }}

==================================================
PREVIOUS STUDENT REMARKS
==================================================

Earlier students' remarks for this instructor and term (newest first, at most 100; remark text and tone only). They are already processed: use them only as evidence for the student interpretation. Never take keywords from them and never use them for overall_tone.

{{ JSON.stringify($json.previous_remarks || []) }}

==================================================
NEW STUDENT FEEDBACK
==================================================

{{ $json.new_student_remark }}

==================================================
IMPORTANT ANALYSIS RULES
==================================================

1. Do not ignore the existing AI analysis.

2. Do not completely replace the existing analysis with information from only the new student.

3. Treat the existing AI analysis as the previous accumulated analysis.

4. Treat the new student feedback as additional evidence.

5. Update the analysis only when the new feedback provides relevant information.

6. Do not invent information.

7. Do not remove valid information from the existing analysis unless the new evidence clearly contradicts it.

8. The updated analysis should represent BOTH:
   - previous student feedback
   - the new student feedback

9. The new student feedback must influence the result when it contains meaningful information.

10. If the new feedback is positive, incorporate its positive information.

11. If the new feedback identifies an improvement area, incorporate that improvement area.

12. The overall tone should represent the NEW student feedback, not the entire historical dataset.

==================================================
STUDENT INTERPRETATION
==================================================

Write an UPDATED OVERALL interpretation of what ALL students are saying, not only the new student.

"student_interpretation" is the summary the instructor reads under "What Your Students Are Saying".

Write ONE paragraph of 5 to 8 complete sentences (about 120 to 200 words) in plain English.

Summarise what students say across ALL the evidence: the EXISTING AI ANALYSIS (its student_interpretation is the previous summary), the PREVIOUS STUDENT REMARKS and the NEW STUDENT FEEDBACK.

Cover:
- what students praise most, and how common it is ("most students", "several students", "a few students");
- the main concerns or requests (for example pacing, examples, grading, attitude);
- specific things students mention, such as teaching methods or class activities;
- the overall mood of the comments (mostly positive, mixed, or critical).

Summarise Bisaya/Cebuano and Tagalog comments in English.

Rules:
- Never use an instructor name or a student name.
- Never invent anything: every statement must be supported by the evidence. When there are too few comments for 5 sentences, write fewer sentences instead of inventing.
- Never quote a vulgar or sexual word, or a masked word (asterisks such as ****).
- No bullet points, no numbering, no headings, no line breaks.
- Do not mention AI, surveys, batches, historical or previous data, updates, or the word cloud.

Rewrite the previous summary so it also reflects the new feedback; do not just add a sentence about the new student.

==================================================
POSITIVE THEMES
==================================================

Update the positive themes based on the existing analysis and the new feedback.

Keep existing valid themes.

Add a new theme only when the new feedback supports it.

Avoid duplicates and different phrases describing the same concept.

Return "positive_themes" as a JSON array of 3 to 5 short, complete sentences.

Each sentence is one separate point: a full sentence in plain English that ends with a period.

Never one long paragraph, never comma-joined fragments, never bullets or numbering inside a sentence.

Never use an instructor name. Do not invent information.

The existing AI analysis may hold this as one paragraph or as separate lines: use it only as evidence and write it again as separate sentences, merged with the new evidence.

==================================================
IMPROVEMENT INSIGHTS
==================================================

Update the improvement insights based on the existing analysis and the new feedback.

Keep existing valid insights.

Add a new insight only when the new feedback supports it.

Avoid duplicates and different phrases describing the same concept.

Return "improvement_insights" as a JSON array of 3 to 5 short, complete sentences.

Each sentence is one separate point: a full sentence in plain English that ends with a period.

Never one long paragraph, never comma-joined fragments, never bullets or numbering inside a sentence.

Never use an instructor name. Do not invent information.

The existing AI analysis may hold this as one paragraph or as separate lines: use it only as evidence and write it again as separate sentences, merged with the new evidence.

==================================================
AI SUGGESTION
==================================================

Create an UPDATED instructor suggestion.

The suggestion must consider both the existing analysis and the new student feedback.

Do not simply copy the existing suggestion.

If the new feedback provides a new improvement area, incorporate it naturally.

If the new feedback only reinforces an existing issue, strengthen the existing recommendation rather than creating a duplicate recommendation.

The suggestion should be concise, professional, constructive, and suitable for an instructor evaluation report.

==================================================
OVERALL TONE
==================================================

Determine the tone of the NEW student feedback.

First understand what the remark means, in ANY language: English, Tagalog, Bisaya/Cebuano, Hiligaynon, Ilocano, Taglish and Bislish mixes, other languages, slang, misspellings, text-speak and emojis. Translate it to English in your head before deciding. Never decide from one keyword.

The value MUST be exactly one of:

Positive
Critical
Neutral

Positive:
Mainly praise, thanks or satisfaction. A "keep it up" or "more of the same" request is still Positive.

Critical:
Any complaint, problem, unmet need, or request to change something. Request markers include unta, sana, dapat, palihug, please, pls, "mas maayo kung", "sana po". Negated praise (dili maayo, hindi malinaw, not clear) and sarcasm ("galing mo sir, wala kaming natutunan") are Critical too.

Praise plus a specific problem or request:
Critical.

Neutral:
Factual, unclear, off-topic, only a greeting, or too short to judge.

Emoji only:
Judge by the meaning of the emoji.

Examples:

"Maayo kaayo mo explain si ma'am."
→ Positive

"Ang galing magturo ni sir, sobrang linaw."
→ Positive

"Salamat sa pasensya, sir!"
→ Positive

"Keep it up po!"
→ Positive

"Very approachable and fair."
→ Positive

"Muy buen profesor."
→ Positive

"Paspas kaayo mo discuss, dili mi ka sabay."
→ Critical

"Sana po bagalan ang pagtuturo."
→ Critical

"Dugangi pa unta ang examples."
→ Critical

"Maayo ra man siya pero kanunay late."
→ Critical

"Galing mo sir, wala kaming natutunan."
→ Critical

"Hindi po malinaw ang grading."
→ Critical

"Mas maayo unta kung naay review before exam."
→ Critical

"Okay ra."
→ Neutral

"Every MWF ang klase."
→ Neutral

==================================================
WORDCLOUD
==================================================

Extract meaningful keywords from the NEW student feedback.

Maximum 5 keywords.

You must return AT LEAST 1 keyword, even if the feedback is vague, short, or emotional.

If the feedback does not contain a specific concrete theme, extract the closest general theme it relates to, such as:
"Teaching quality"
"Attitude"
"Fairness"
"Communication"
"Professionalism"
"Classroom management"

Only return zero keywords if the feedback text is completely empty or unreadable.

Each keyword must contain 1–3 words.

Normalize Tagalog and Bisaya/Cebuano concepts into concise English themes when appropriate.

Remove filler words.

Never use a vulgar or sexual word, or a masked word (asterisks such as ****), as a keyword.

Remove meaningless emotional words on their own (e.g. do not return just "Bad" or "Good"), but you may still capture the underlying theme those words point to (e.g. "Teaching quality").

Do not use vague keywords such as:
"Good"
"Nice"
"Okay"
"Instructor"
unless the word represents a meaningful theme.

==================================================
WORDCLOUD DUPLICATE RULE
==================================================

The EXISTING WORDCLOUD contains previously stored concepts.

If the new feedback represents the SAME concept as an existing word, use the EXISTING WORD exactly.

Example:

Existing word:
"Examples"

New feedback:
"Please provide more examples."

Correct:
"Examples"

Incorrect:
"More examples"

Another example:

Existing word:
"Teaching clarity"

New feedback:
"Maayo kaayo mo explain."

Correct:
"Teaching clarity"

Do NOT create duplicate concepts such as:
"Clear explanation"
"Good explanation"
"Explanation clarity"
if "Teaching clarity" already exists.

Every returned keyword must have:
"count": 1

The database will add this count to the existing wordcloud.

==================================================
OUTPUT FORMAT
==================================================

Return ONLY valid JSON.

Do NOT return:
- Markdown
- ```json
- Explanation
- Comments
- Extra text

Use exactly this structure:

{
  "ai_suggestion": "Updated instructor suggestion...",
  "student_interpretation": "One paragraph of 5 to 8 complete sentences summarising what all students say.",
  "positive_themes": [
    "The instructor explains difficult topics clearly.",
    "The lessons are well prepared and organized.",
    "Grading is fair and consistent."
  ],
  "improvement_insights": [
    "More worked examples would help students follow the lessons.",
    "The pace of some discussions could be slower.",
    "Quizzes could be shorter."
  ],
  "overall_tone": "Critical",
  "keywords": [
    {
      "word": "Teaching clarity",
      "count": 1
    },
    {
      "word": "Examples",
      "count": 1
    }
  ]
}

IMPORTANT:
- overall_tone MUST be exactly Positive, Critical, or Neutral.
- student_interpretation MUST be ONE paragraph of 5 to 8 complete sentences about ALL students (existing analysis, previous remarks and the new feedback), not only the new student.
- keywords MUST be an array.
- keywords MUST contain at least 1 item.
- Maximum 5 keywords.
- Every keyword count MUST be 1.
- Do not invent keywords unrelated to the feedback.
- Do not invent information.
- Return valid JSON only.

-- Get Previous Instructor Analysis1. The new remark is stored after the AI call, so it is not in here.
-- Parameters: instructor id, term id.
SELECT
    p.instructor_id,
    p.term_id,
    ai.ai_suggestion,
    ai.student_interpretation,
    ai.positive_themes,
    ai.improvement_insights,
    ai.overall_tone,
    COALESCE(
        (
            SELECT jsonb_agg(
                jsonb_build_object('remark', x.remark, 'tone', x.tone)
                ORDER BY x.created_at DESC
            )
            FROM (
                SELECT sr.remark, sr.tone, sr.created_at
                FROM public.student_remarks sr
                WHERE sr.instructor_id = p.instructor_id
                  AND sr.term_id = p.term_id
                ORDER BY sr.created_at DESC
                LIMIT 100

        '[]'::jsonb

FROM (SELECT $1::uuid AS instructor_id, $2::uuid AS term_id) p
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT s.ai_suggestion, s.student_interpretation, s.positive_themes, s.improvement_insights, s.overall_tone
    FROM public.instructor_ai_suggestions s
    WHERE s.instructor_id = p.instructor_id
      AND s.term_id = p.term_id
    LIMIT 1
) ai ON true;

-- Scores the form's instructor/subject; Decide adds token scores and applies the thresholds.
WITH
prm AS (
  SELECT lower(btrim(COALESCE($1, ''))) AS batch_iid,
         lower(btrim(COALESCE($2, ''))) AS batch_sid,
         btrim(COALESCE($3, ''))        AS ocr_i,
         btrim(COALESCE($4, ''))        AS ocr_s,
         COALESCE(
           NULLIF(btrim(COALESCE($5, '')), ''),
           (SELECT ss.current_term_id::text
              FROM public.system_settings ss
             ORDER BY (ss.id::text = '1') DESC
             LIMIT 1)
         ) AS term_id
),
cand AS (
  SELECT ui.id::text                                                                AS id,
         btrim(COALESCE(ui.first_name, ''))                                         AS first_name,
         btrim(COALESCE(ui.last_name, ''))                                          AS last_name,
         lower(COALESCE(ui.is_placeholder::text, 'false')) IN ('true', 't', '1', 'yes') AS is_placeholder,
         (ui.id::text = p.batch_iid)                                                AS is_batch,
         COALESCE(ui.account_status = 'approved', false)                            AS approved
  FROM public.user_info ui
  CROSS JOIN prm p
  WHERE ui.id::text = p.batch_iid
     OR lower(COALESCE(ui.is_placeholder::text, 'false')) IN ('true', 't', '1', 'yes')
     OR ( ui.account_status = 'approved'
          AND EXISTS (SELECT 1
                        FROM public.department_table dt
                        JOIN public.roles r ON r.id = dt.roles
                       WHERE dt.user_id = ui.id
                         AND r."Roles" IN ('DEPARTMENT_HEAD', 'FULL-TIME', 'PART-TIME')) )
),
txt AS (
  SELECT 'o'::text AS kind, ''::text AS id, p.ocr_i AS t FROM prm p
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'f', c.id, c.first_name FROM cand c
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'l', c.id, c.last_name FROM cand c
),
-- no unaccent on Supabase, so accents are folded with translate
nrm AS (
  SELECT x.kind, x.id,
         btrim(regexp_replace(
           regexp_replace(
             regexp_replace(
               regexp_replace(
                 lower(translate(x.t,
                   'ÁÀÂÄÃÅĀáàâäãåāÉÈÊËĒéèêëēÍÌÎÏĪíìîïīÓÒÔÖÕŌóòôöõōÚÙÛÜŪúùûüūÑñÇç',
                   'AAAAAAAaaaaaaaEEEEEeeeeeIIIIIiiiiiOOOOOOooooooUUUUUuuuuuNnCc')),
                 '\mma[''’‘`´]?am\M', ' maam ', 'g'),
               '[^a-z]+', ' ', 'g'),
             '\m(prof|professor|dr|doc|mr|mrs|ms|miss|madam|maam|sir|engr|eng|atty|arch|rev|fr|hon|instr|instructor|teacher|phd|edd|dba|mba|mit|mat|maed|lpt|rn|cpa|jr|sr|ii|iii|iv)\M',
             ' ', 'g'),
           '\s+', ' ', 'g')) AS n
  FROM txt x
),
o AS (
  SELECT n.n                                   AS n,
         string_to_array(n.n, ' ')             AS toks,
         length(replace(n.n, ' ', ''))         AS letters
  FROM nrm n
  WHERE n.kind = 'o'
),
cn AS (
  SELECT c.*, f.n AS nf, l.n AS nl, btrim(f.n || ' ' || l.n) AS nfull
  FROM cand c
  JOIN nrm f ON f.kind = 'f' AND f.id = c.id
  JOIN nrm l ON l.kind = 'l' AND l.id = c.id
),
sims AS (
  SELECT cn.*,
         o.n AS o_n,
         round(similarity(cn.nfull, o.n)::numeric, 4)                                    AS sim,
         round(word_similarity(cn.nl, o.n)::numeric, 4)                                  AS last_ws,
         round(GREATEST(word_similarity(cn.nf, o.n),
                        word_similarity(split_part(cn.nf, ' ', 1), o.n))::numeric, 4)    AS first_ws,
         ( cn.nl <> '' AND o.n <> ''
           AND ( string_to_array(cn.nl, ' ') <@ o.toks
                 OR replace(cn.nl, ' ', '') = ANY (o.toks) ) )                           AS last_whole,
         ( cn.nf <> '' AND left(cn.nf, 1) = ANY (o.toks) )                               AS initial_hit,
         ( cn.nl <> '' AND o.n = cn.nl )                                                 AS surname_only
  FROM cn
  CROSS JOIN o
),
hits AS (
  SELECT s.*,
         ( s.nl <> '' AND s.o_n <> '' AND (s.last_whole OR s.last_ws >= 0.8) )          AS last_hit,
         ( s.nf <> '' AND s.o_n <> '' AND s.first_ws >= 0.7 )                            AS first_hit
  FROM sims s
),
scored AS (
  SELECT h.*,
         CASE WHEN h.o_n = ''                   THEN 0::numeric
              WHEN h.last_hit AND h.first_hit   THEN GREATEST(0.95, h.sim)
              WHEN h.last_hit AND h.initial_hit THEN 0.85
              WHEN h.surname_only               THEN 0.70
              WHEN h.last_hit                   THEN GREATEST(0.60, h.sim)
              ELSE h.sim
         END AS score
  FROM hits h
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT s.*,
         row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s.score DESC, s.is_batch DESC, s.approved DESC,
                                     s.last_name, s.first_name, s.id) AS rn
  FROM scored s
),
os AS (
  SELECT p.ocr_s                                                                    AS raw,
         upper(regexp_replace(p.ocr_s, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'))                    AS alnum,
         upper(regexp_replace(COALESCE(substring(p.ocr_s from '\(([^()]*)\)[^()]*$'), ''),
                              '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'))                             AS paren_alnum,
         btrim(regexp_replace(lower(translate(p.ocr_s,
                   'ÁÀÂÄÃÅĀáàâäãåāÉÈÊËĒéèêëēÍÌÎÏĪíìîïīÓÒÔÖÕŌóòôöõōÚÙÛÜŪúùûüūÑñÇç',
                   'AAAAAAAaaaaaaaEEEEEeeeeeIIIIIiiiiiOOOOOOooooooUUUUUuuuuuNnCc')),
                              '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))                              AS n
  FROM prm p
),
keys AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT k.key
  FROM (
    SELECT m[1] || m[2] AS key
      FROM os, regexp_matches(upper(os.raw), '([A-Z]{2,8})[ .-]?([0-9]{1,4}[A-Z]?)', 'g') AS m
    UNION ALL
    SELECT os.alnum FROM os
    UNION ALL
    SELECT os.paren_alnum FROM os
  ) k
  WHERE length(k.key) >= 3
),
subj AS (
  SELECT s.id::text                                                                 AS id,
         COALESCE(s.subject_code, '')                                               AS code,
         COALESCE(s.subject_name, '')                                               AS name,
         (s.id::text = p.batch_sid)                                                 AS is_batch,
         upper(regexp_replace(COALESCE(s.subject_code, ''), '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g')) AS code_key,
         btrim(regexp_replace(lower(translate(COALESCE(s.subject_name, ''),
                   'ÁÀÂÄÃÅĀáàâäãåāÉÈÊËĒéèêëēÍÌÎÏĪíìîïīÓÒÔÖÕŌóòôöõōÚÙÛÜŪúùûüūÑñÇç',
                   'AAAAAAAaaaaaaaEEEEEeeeeeIIIIIiiiiiOOOOOOooooooUUUUUuuuuuNnCc')),
                              '[^a-z0-9]+', ' ', 'g'))                              AS nname
  FROM public.subjects s
  CROSS JOIN prm p
),
sscore AS (
  SELECT sb.*,
         ( sb.code_key <> '' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM keys WHERE keys.key = sb.code_key) ) AS code_hit,
         CASE WHEN os.n = '' OR sb.nname = '' THEN 0::numeric
              ELSE round(GREATEST(similarity(sb.nname, os.n),
                                  word_similarity(sb.nname, os.n))::numeric, 4)
         END AS name_score,
         COALESCE((SELECT jsonb_agg(DISTINCT lower(isub.instructor_id::text))
                     FROM public.instructor_subjects isub
                    WHERE isub.subject_id::text = sb.id
                      AND isub.instructor_id IS NOT NULL
                      AND isub.term_id::text = p.term_id), '[]'::jsonb)             AS linked_instructor_ids
  FROM subj sb
  CROSS JOIN os
  CROSS JOIN prm p
),
sranked AS (
  SELECT x.*,
         row_number() OVER (ORDER BY x.code_hit DESC, x.name_score DESC, x.is_batch DESC,
                                     x.code, x.id) AS rn
  FROM sscore x
)
SELECT
  1                                                                                AS form_match_version,
  (SELECT o.n FROM o)                                                              AS ocr_instructor_norm,
  (SELECT o.letters FROM o)                                                        AS ocr_instructor_letters,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cand c WHERE c.is_batch)                                   AS batch_instructor_found,
  COALESCE((SELECT btrim(c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name) FROM cand c WHERE c.is_batch LIMIT 1), '')
                                                                                   AS batch_instructor_name,
  COALESCE((SELECT r.score FROM ranked r WHERE r.is_batch LIMIT 1), 0)::float8     AS batch_instructor_score,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
            'id', r.id,
            'name', btrim(r.first_name || ' ' || r.last_name),
            'score', r.score,
            'is_placeholder', r.is_placeholder,
            'is_batch', r.is_batch) ORDER BY r.rn), '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM ranked r
    WHERE r.rn <= 300 OR r.is_batch)                                                AS instructor_candidates,
  (SELECT os.n FROM os)                                                            AS ocr_subject_norm,
  (SELECT length(os.alnum) FROM os)                                                AS ocr_subject_alnum_len,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM subj s WHERE s.is_batch)                                   AS batch_subject_found,
  COALESCE((SELECT s.code FROM subj s WHERE s.is_batch LIMIT 1), '')               AS batch_subject_code,
  COALESCE((SELECT s.name FROM subj s WHERE s.is_batch LIMIT 1), '')               AS batch_subject_name,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
            'id', r.id,
            'code', r.code,
            'name', r.name,
            'code_hit', r.code_hit,
            'name_score', r.name_score,
            'score', CASE WHEN r.code_hit THEN 1 ELSE r.name_score END,
            'is_batch', r.is_batch,
            'linked_instructor_ids', r.linked_instructor_ids) ORDER BY r.rn), '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM sranked r
    WHERE r.rn <= 300 OR r.is_batch)                                                AS subject_candidates,
  (SELECT p.term_id FROM prm p)                                                    AS term_id
FROM prm;

INSERT INTO public.sheet_import_jobs (status, rows, matched, unmatched, error_count, message, n8n_execution_id, requested_by)
VALUES (
  'processing',
  $1::int,
  $2::int,
  $3::int,
  $3::int,
  'Import started: saving the rows and running the AI remark analysis.',
  NULLIF($4::text, ''),
  NULLIF($5::text, '')::uuid
)
RETURNING id;

-- Google Sheet import job (migration 018): the whole flow has finished. Real counts; 'done' unless a
-- failure was recorded ('Mark Import Job Failed' or found by the summary), which stays 'error'.
-- Parameters: job id, rows, matched, unmatched, imported, errors, AI groups, AI failed,
-- has problems, first failed node, message.
UPDATE public.sheet_import_jobs
   SET status = CASE WHEN status = 'error' OR $9::boolean THEN 'error' ELSE 'done' END,
       rows = $2::int,
       matched = $3::int,
       unmatched = $4::int,
       imported_count = $5::int,
       error_count = $6::int,
       ai_groups = $7::int,
       ai_failed = $8::int,
       failed_node = COALESCE(failed_node, NULLIF($10::text, '')),
       message = CASE WHEN status = 'error' AND message IS NOT NULL AND failed_node IS NOT NULL
                      THEN message || ' ' || $11::text
                      ELSE $11::text END,
       finished_at = now()
 WHERE id = $1::uuid
   AND finished_at IS NULL;

-- Google Sheet import job (migration 018): a step after the early answer failed. The first failure
-- keeps its node and message; the import goes on, 'Mark Import Job Done' sets finished_at later.
-- Parameters: n8n execution id, failed node, message. No job row (phone, website, correction): no-op.
UPDATE public.sheet_import_jobs
   SET status = 'error',
       failed_node = COALESCE(failed_node, $2::text),
       message = CASE WHEN failed_node IS NULL THEN $3::text ELSE message END
 WHERE n8n_execution_id = $1::text
   AND finished_at IS NULL;

-- Google Sheet import job (migration 018): the execution itself failed (a node without an error
-- output threw, Stop and Error, a timeout). Run by this workflow's own Error Trigger.
-- Parameters: failed execution id, last node executed, message. Not a sheet import: no-op.
UPDATE public.sheet_import_jobs
   SET status = 'error',
       failed_node = COALESCE(NULLIF($2::text, ''), failed_node),
       message = $3::text,
       finished_at = now()
 WHERE n8n_execution_id = NULLIF($1::text, '')
   AND finished_at IS NULL;

-- sast-manual-correction: who and what a correction can be credited to, for the LOCAL text match in
-- 'Correction Name Match' (name_match.js). Only for corrections that send names without ids (older
-- app versions); never sent to Gemini. Same people as 'get instructor id7' (approved +
-- DEPARTMENT_HEAD / FULL-TIME / PART-TIME, or a placeholder), one entry per person; every subject.
-- No parameters. Always exactly one row.
WITH
ins AS (
  SELECT ui.id,
         btrim(regexp_replace(btrim(COALESCE(ui.first_name, '')) || ' ' || btrim(COALESCE(ui.last_name, '')),
                              '\s+', ' ', 'g')) AS name
  FROM public.user_info ui
  WHERE (ui.account_status = 'approved'
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1
                       FROM public.department_table dt
                       JOIN public.roles r ON r.id = dt.roles
                      WHERE dt.user_id = ui.id
                        AND r."Roles" IN ('DEPARTMENT_HEAD', 'FULL-TIME', 'PART-TIME')))
     OR lower(COALESCE(ui.is_placeholder::text, 'false')) IN ('true', 't', '1', 'yes')
)
SELECT
  1 AS candidates_version,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('id', i.id, 'name', i.name) ORDER BY lower(i.name), i.id),
                   '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM ins i
    WHERE i.name <> '') AS instructors,
  (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('id', s.id,
                                                'code', btrim(COALESCE(s.subject_code, '')),
                                                'name', btrim(COALESCE(s.subject_name, '')))
                             ORDER BY s.subject_code, s.id),
                   '[]'::jsonb)
     FROM public.subjects s) AS subjects;
